To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the low SNR behavior of non-coherent channels with memory is determined by the rate of decay of the autocorrelation of the fading process, and that for slowly decaying processes IID signaling is optimal whereas for quickly decaying processes block-constant signaling is optimal.

the low SNR channel capacity is achieved by a) IID inputs for channels in the slowly forgetting family and b) inputs with IID phase and block-constant magnitude for channels in the quickly forgetting family.

the low SNR channel capacity of a non-coherent fading channel with memory under a power constraint can be approached by IID inputs if and only if the fading process is slowly forgetting, and that it can be approached by non-IID inputs otherwise.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: (1) What is the capacity of a non-coherent fading channel under a peak-power (rather than an average-power) constraint, and how does the capacity grow as the SNR tends to 0?
the low SNR behavior of peak-limited non-coherent fading channels with memory.
the low SNR regime of fading channels with memory.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
for channels in the ``quickly-forgetting'' category the capacity-achieving input is block constant in phase and magnitude, and the capacity growth rate is equal to the prediction error growth rate.
, in the low SNR regime, the capacity of a peak-limited fading channel is achieved by IID input symbols with a phase distribution that is optimal for the corresponding noiseless channel.

the asymptotic behavior (as SNR goes to 0) of channel capacity is the same for slowly forgetting channels and for quickly forgetting channels, and that it is achieved by the same inputs for slowly forgetting channels as by the inputs with IID phase and block-constant magnitude for quickly forgetting channels.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the capacity of non-coherently demodulated fading channels is achieved asymptotically in two different ways: either by IID inputs or by inputs with block-constant magnitude, depending on whether the fading law is slowly or quickly forgetting.
the low SNR behavior of channel capacity is determined by the fading process, and not by the input.

the low-SNR capacity of non-coherently detected channels with memory is achieved by the following input distribution: IID phase, block-constant magnitude, blockwise independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) magnitude.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for slowly forgetting fading laws, the low SNR asymptotic capacity is achieved by the same class of input distributions (IID) as the high SNR asymptotic one.

the low SNR behavior of the capacity of peak-power constrained non-coherent fading channels with memory is determined by the fading law, and that this behavior is independent of the peak-power constraint.
, in the low SNR regime, the capacity is achieved by a simple coding strategy, and the capacity growth rate is governed by the rate at which the channel fades away.
